m0555: Count as confirmed dead target, retaining creature or player type; direct damage, projectiles, explosions with a clear igniter, tamed pets with identifiable owners, and sustained burning with traced ignition sources can be attributed. Non-death, totem life-saving, cancellation and repeated death paths are not counted; environmental deaths do not borrow from the nearest attacker, and player kills are not counted when the source cannot be reliably identified.
m0556: The old version may miss the withering settlement and pet kill after the killer goes offline; the history retains the original algorithm and there is no speculative backfilling. The current version only continues ownership if the confirmed source, target and owner identities still match.
m0557: The pet's owner identity saved with the world can be used across game processes, and the pet's original owner will still be checked when attributing. The old algorithm could miss pet kills while the owner was offline after a restart.
m0558: Record new crops actually formed from seeds or plantable items, classified by adapted crops; fertilization, natural growth, failure, and cancellation are not counted.
m0559: Only the newborn individuals that have actually joined the world in the original mating results are recorded, classified by offspring type and birth dimension. Both parents must belong to the same player; they will not be distributed repeatedly if fed by different players or the source cannot be confirmed. Feeding, love, cooldown, cancellation, command generation, and mere pregnancy or spawning are not counted; confirmed feeding sources can be carried over to births after the player is offline during this run.
m0560: Only record the final successful submission of the player's backpack or workspace synthesis on the server, including recipe book operations. The number of synthesis times is accumulated according to the number of times the recipe is executed, and the products are accumulated according to the actual number of recipes; one batch operation can contain multiple recipes. Previews, moving materials, rollback on failure, directly giving items, and automatic synthesizers do not count. The times are classified according to the first product of the formula; the product details include bottles, barrels and other containers returned by the formula.
m0561: Only the results of successful transactions between villagers and wandering merchants in the original version are recorded. The number of transactions and the number of products are accumulated separately, and classified according to the actual product type. Multiple transactions can be completed in one batch operation; opening interface, preview, failed rollback, sold out and plug-in economic transactions are not counted.
m0562: Retracting the pole is counted according to the actual operation completed by the server, including empty retracting. Pulling back an item requires that the object entity actually experiences pulling force, and pulling back a creature is not considered an item; successful fishing requires that fishing products that are newly generated and confirmed to enter the world during this fishing rod retrieval, and hooking existing items are not counted as new fish catches. The number of operations and the number of items are accumulated separately. Generating a fish catch does not mean that it has been picked up and put into the backpack. Rod retrieval is classified by fishhook, and pulling back and fishing are classified by item type; when there are multiple items in the same operation, the times are classified into the first item sorted by identification, and the quantities are listed separately.
m0563: Movement distance is an estimate of the server's adjacent location. Each segment is only classified into one mode of movement, including vehicle, gliding, flying, swimming and walking. Walking uses horizontal distances, and the rest uses three-dimensional distances. Teleportation, interdimensionality, rebirth, mode switching and abnormal jumps will cut off distance accumulation.
m0564: Active time is estimated from confirmed movement input with displacement, digging, interaction, or public speaking. By default, the accumulation will stop after 5 consecutive minutes of no valid behavior. The online stay time includes hanging up and is recorded separately.
m0565: The selected records have an idle threshold of {0}.
m0566: Reach the adapted mature state before destruction, and record it after successful destruction; this is the number of blocks harvested, not the number of dropped objects. The upper and lower squares of mature Sarracenia are counted separately, immature crops and melon vines are not counted, and both survival and creation operations are recorded.
m0567: Record the number of operations to change the status of sweet berries and glowing berries after they are actually harvested; repeated clicks on empty fruit, fertilization, failure and cancellation are not counted.
m0568: Count according to the actual destroyed block position, and the paired half-blocks that have been confirmed to disappear at the same time are recorded separately; failures and cancellations are not counted, and the old records retain the original algorithm.
m0569: Count according to the actual number of squares placed. When the bed and door are completely placed, they will be counted as two squares each. m1937: Reports summarize received records in the platform statistics time zone. Missing records do not mean no activity. Today's totals and late-arriving data may still change. Overlapping projects count each action only once in server totals. Reports are not sent to QQ automatically.
m1938: Sampled approximately every 10 seconds, details retained for 30 days; curves summarized by time period, vacancies are not zero. Fluency comes from the game tick interval, which shows up to 20 TPS, not the MSPT that takes a single frame to execute. CPU is the ratio of game processes to all logical cores of the machine, and memory is the working set of game processes. Disconnections, long frames, and restarts are observations and cannot be relied upon to determine the cause of crashes or freezes. The number of blocks and entities have not been collected yet. The whole machine CPU, physical memory and fixed disk space come from the Windows system interface; the network is the total sending and receiving rate of the enabled physical network card, and the virtual/VPN network card is not added repeatedly. The whole machine sampling runs with the game collection plug-in, and monitoring will not continue after the server is stopped. Disk shows space, not read and write speed.
